newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Congo's Djambala field gets development go-ahead.
newsitem.headline: Congo's Djambala field gets development go-ahead.

text.p: South Africa's Sasol Ltd said on Monday that it was going ahead with the development of of its first oil discovcery, the Djambala field some 55 km offshore Congo it which it holds a minority stake.

Sasol unit Sasol Petroleum International (Pty) Ltd holds a 13 percent interest in the field in partnership with national oil company Hydro Congo and Agip Recherches Congo SA which hold 35 and 52 percent respectively. Agip acts as the operator.
A permit for the expliotation of the field was recently granted by the government of Congo and the field is expected to go on stream in record time, less than two years after its discovery.
It will initially produce 4,000 barrels a day of high quality crude and production is scheduled to start in August 1998. Field life is estimated at 10 years.
